From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Sara Li <sara.li@brightmart.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@brightmart.com>

Subject: Re: Vector index harmonization + evaluation matrix for BrightMart onboard

Thanks Sara — received the sample. High level answers up front so the kickoff is productive:

1) ANN recommendation: HNSW for recall-first pilot, PQ-compressed OPQ or IVF-PQ for cost-constrained production. We'll size initial shards to ~250k vectors per shard (NVIDIA and cloud best practices) and iterate based on query QPS.

2) Backfill vs incremental: For the 12M catalog I recommend a two-wave approach: a) cold seed backfill (bulk async job) into a staging index, b) warm incremental delta ingestion with the streaming pipeline for real-time updates. Backfill ETA: ~36 hours on our Dedicated cluster with parallel workers (estimate; dependent on CSV cleanup).

3) Rerank evals: We'll share an evaluation matrix (attached: onboard-eval-matrix.xlsx). Plan: hold baseline set (1000 queries sampled by user intent buckets), run embed+ANN retrieval, then run reranker candidates with the same prompt sets and compute NDCG/MRR + qualitative pass on top-20. We'll include sampling notes for multi-lingual coverage.

Kickoff: 9/16 11am PT works for our team. I'll send calendar invite. Pre-kickoff asks: please confirm primary key for SKUs (Tom), and let us know acceptable downtime window for index cutover.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai

Tom — quick suggestions from ops:

- Legacy SKUs: map legacy -> product_sku via a best-effort join table. For rows with no match, inject a synthetic \"legacy_id:<hash>\" as a stable PK and tag records for downstream cleanup; treat these as low-confidence during rerank evals.
- Tokenization: use language-aware tokenizer (we recommend model tokenizer matching the embedder). For cross-lingual consistency, we suggest a joint multilingual embedder (we have validated M-BERT-derived and open LLaMA variants). Expect vector dims 768–1024 depending on model; larger dims increase storage and ANN latency.
- Cost/time: backfill throughput estimate ~120k vectors/hour per worker; we'll provide a parallel worker plan in the kickoff.

Action items I can own for kickoff: produce shard sizing table, draft backfill worker config, and prepare a short runbook for safe brownout cutover. Adding Marissa to coordinate CSM acceptance criteria and evaluation buckets.

—Monica
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
